info.bio:
"Chubby" Checker (1941), llamado chubby por su generosidad de carnes, es el rey del twist. Llevó al éxito masivo la composición de Hank Ballard "the twist" en 1960.

El baile que llevaba incorporado fue un auténtico fenómeno de masas, del que ninguna capa social se libró. Al año siguiente repetiría éxito con su "let´s twist again".

Si bien lo intentó repetir con otros bailes como el limbo o el hunckleback su estrella se apagaría pronto.

scenes.name: Pauline Boty y el pop art británico
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Pintora pop con una perspectiva femenina: collages a partir de canciones pop («Target for Twisters», «Goodbye Cruel World»), cuadros de Monica Vitti, Belmondo o Marilyn, My Colouring Book (a partir de la canción de Kitty Kallen), 5–4–3–2–1 (por la sintonía de Ready Steady Go!, donde bailaba) o Scandal 63 con Christine Keeler. Protagonizó con Peter Blake, Derek Boshier y Peter Phillips el Monitor «Pop Goes the Easel» de Ken Russell (1962) y fue la entrevistada estrella de Talking to Women: vivía como si le quedaran pocos años, «porque la bomba iba a caer». It’s a Man’s World I y II (1964-1965) respondían desde el otro lado al tema que James Brown convirtió en balada torturada en 1966. Rechazó abortar para tratar su cáncer y murió el 1 de julio de 1966, cuando el disco de Dusty entraba en el Top 10 americano; no tuvo reconocimiento en vida.

scenes.name: Del Twist al Boo-Ga-Loo: bailes y discotecas
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: El Twist (1960-1962) fue el gran liberador del baile social: sin pareja, libre, con poco juego de pies; tras él llegó un aluvión de bailes nacidos entre adolescentes negros y popularizados por músicos negros (el Pony, el Watusi, el Mashed Potato, el Frug, el Monkey, el Jerk), cuyo nombre iba en el título del disco. Supusieron la vuelta del cuerpo a la cultura popular blanca. Los institucionalizaron las discotecas (el Whisky a Go Go del Sunset Strip, enero de 1964, con chicas bailando en jaulas) y los programas de televisión (Shindig!, Hullabaloo, Where the Action Is). «Land of 1000 Dances», de Chris Kenner (1962), enumeraba los bailes; Cannibal & the Headhunters, del este de Los Ángeles, le añadieron el «na na-ne-na-na» en 1965. En 1966 llegó el Boo-Ga-Loo de Tom and Jerrio, mezcla de Motown, aire latino y gritos a lo James Brown, en la estela de «Let’s Dance» de Chris Montez y «Wooly Bully» de Sam the Sham, el single más vendido de 1965.

podcast.title: Bitterness and Perceived Erasure from History
podcast.body: In recent decades, Chubby Checker has expressed significant bitterness and felt overlooked regarding his place in rock and roll history, despite his massive commercial success. He is convinced there is an attempt to erase him from the genre's narrative and believes he deserves the same prominence as figures like Elvis Presley and The Beatles. "Recent interviews show that Checker is convinced he is the victim of an attempt to erase him from rock and roll history, and believes he deserves equal prominence with Elvis and the Beatles."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Claims of Racism and Hall of Fame Omission
podcast.body: Checker attributes his lack of recognition, particularly his non-induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, to racism. He specifically points to his marriage to a white woman as a contributing factor. He has publicly protested outside the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame regarding this perceived oversight. "He believes his lack of recognition is down to racism, as he married a white woman and has protested outside the rock and roll whole of fame at his lack of induction."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Dick Clark's Christmas Card Recording
podcast.body: Before his success with "The Twist," Ernest Evans recorded an audio Christmas card for Dick Clark's friends. This private recording featured Evans singing jingle bells while performing impressions of various singers, including Fats Domino, Elvis Presley, and The Chipmunks. A later public re-recording as a duet with Bobby Rydell included these same impressions. "Evan said told the people at Cameo Parkway he could do impressions of different singers, and so they'd ask him to record it."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Dick Clark's Promotion for "The Twist"
podcast.body: Dick Clark deliberately chose Chubby Checker to remake "The Twist" instead of Hank Ballard. Clark sought a performer who was known to him, "unthreatening" (which is generally considered to have meant "less obviously black"), younger, not associated with an "adult act," and with whom Clark might have financial connections. Checker's ability to do impressions and perform in the style of Ballard made him an easy choice. Clark then ensured Checker performed a toned-down, television-appropriate version of the dance on his shows. "So when Clark wanted a record that sounded exactly like Hank Ballard in the Midnighters singing The Twist, it was easy enough for Chacker to do a Ballard in Fashion."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Hip-Hop Remake of "The Twist"
podcast.body: In the late 1980s, Chubby Checker achieved a novelty hit by collaborating with The Fat Boys on a hip-hop remake of "The Twist." "even scoring a novelty hit in the late 80s with a hip-hop remake of The Twist with the fat boys."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Marriage to Catherine Allodders
podcast.body: In 1964, Chubby Checker married Catherine Allodders, who had been crowned Miss World 1962. Their marriage has proven remarkably enduring, lasting for nearly 60 years to the present day, which is considered unusual for a union between a rock star and a beauty queen. "Rather amazingly from marriage between a rock star and a beauty queen, they remained married to this day nearly 60 years later."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Stage Name Origin
podcast.body: Ernest Evans was given his stage name, Chubby Checa, by Dick Clark's wife, Barbara. This name was a playful reference to Evans' impression of Fats Domino, combining "Chubby" (like "Fats") with "Checa" (a twist on "Domino"). "Dick Clark's wife Barbara was there when he was doing the recording, and she called him Chubby Checa as a play on Fat Stomano."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Unavailable Recordings and Lost Royalties
podcast.body: For a prolonged period, Chubby Checker's most successful records were legally unavailable. After Cameo Parkway was acquired by music industry executive Allen Klein in the late 1960s (reportedly as a tax write-off), the label's recordings went out of print and were not reissued on CD between 1975 and 2005. This meant Checker did not receive royalties he would have otherwise earned from 30 years of nostalgia compilation albums. "And between 1975 and 2005, there was no legal way to get any of the recordings on that label, as they went out of print and weren't issued on CD, so Checker didn't get the royalties he could have been getting from 30 years of nostalgia compilation albums."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
